museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou
title: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works that reorganise the relation between a recognisable subject and a painted surface.
introduction:
A window usually offers a view through something. A painting can do that too, but the works in this selection repeatedly interrupt the passage. Braque's objects break into planes; Kandinsky's colours need no objects at all; a painted wooden head by Taeuber-Arp makes likeness coexist with conspicuous construction.

These are different choices, not successive rungs on a ladder towards abstraction. Valadon's reclining woman and Balthus's courtyard retain recognisable rooms while asking how a figure or a frame controls our access to them. Across the selection, the useful question is where the eye is allowed to travel and where it meets the surface. The guide concerns collection works, not their current exhibition locations.
visitNote: The Centre Pompidou's Paris building is closed for renovation, with reopening planned for 2030. Follow the linked museum information for its programme at other venues. This guide concerns the collection and is not a route through currently open Paris galleries.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by Michael Sadleir
books.note: Concerning the Spiritual in Art gives Kandinsky's own account of his ambitions for colour and abstract form. It is a historical argument by one artist, useful beside these works but not a rulebook for every artist in the selection.

works.title: A Red Pedestal
works.credit: Georges Braque. A Red Pedestal. WikiArt source label: Georges Braque Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/georges-braque/a-red-pedestal-1939
works.license: Georges Braque Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The stand gives Braque's overlapping planes something to gather around. Vessels remain recognisable, but their positions do not resolve into an entirely consistent view. The red vertical area repeatedly returns attention to the tall structure. It functions as an anchor without cancelling the smaller uncertainties through which each object meets its neighbours.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Bust of a Young Woman from Avignon
works.catalogueTitle: Bust of young woman from Avignon
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Bust of young woman from Avignon. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/bust-of-young-woman-from-avignon-1907
works.description: Dark contours divide the face into separate areas instead of smoothing its surfaces into continuous flesh. The broad shoulder and turned head still establish a bust, but the construction makes the familiar format difficult to take for granted. Picasso preserves enough of the figure to register how strongly its parts have been made to resist a unified viewpoint.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Fruit Dish
works.medium: Charcoal, gouache and oil on canvas
works.credit: Georges Braque. Fruit Dish. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/georges-braque/fruit-dish-1913
works.description: A dish, fruit and table must be assembled from incomplete clues. Lines continue across areas whose tones or textures pull them back towards the flat surface. Braque permits both readings to remain active: the marks indicate objects, yet their arrangement is never merely a transparent view of those objects. The effort of recognition becomes part of looking.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Lolotte
works.credit: Amedeo Modigliani. Lolotte. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/amedeo-modigliani/lolotte-1916
works.description: The long neck extends the portrait's vertical movement between dark clothing and red hair. Modigliani repeats curves without making the face perfectly symmetrical or interchangeable. Small differences in the eyes and mouth interrupt the larger regularity. The portrait holds a particular sitter within an openly stylised construction rather than asking elongation to pass unnoticed as natural proportion.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Memory of the Halls of Mirrors in Brussels
works.catalogueTitle: Memory of the Halls of Mirrors in Brussels
works.credit: Otto Dix. Memory of the Halls of Mirrors in Brussels. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/otto-dix/memory-of-the-halls-of-mirrors-in-brussels
works.description: Mirrors should multiply a room, but here multiplication makes the room harder to reconstruct. Figures, furnishings and reflected fragments meet at abrupt angles. Dix leaves few reliable passages through the crowded interior. The title names a memory, not an architectural survey; the broken arrangement allows a scene to remain insistent without becoming spatially coherent.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Yellow-Red-Blue
works.credit: Wassily Kandinsky. Yellow-Red-Blue. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The left and right halves behave differently. Angular yellow forms spread on one side, while darker circular masses and curling lines gather on the other; red areas help negotiate their meeting. Kandinsky does not need a depicted event to establish movement. Unequal weights and contrasting kinds of edge make the eye continually reconsider the balance.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Paranoiac Woman-Horse
works.catalogueTitle: Paranoiac Woman-Horse (Invisible Sleeping Woman, Lion, Horse)
works.credit: Salvador Dalí. Paranoiac Woman-Horse (Invisible Sleeping Woman, Lion, Horse). WikiArt source label: Salvador Dali Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/salvador-dali/paranoiac-woman-horse-invisible-sleeping-woman-lion-horse
works.license: Salvador Dali Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The shadows seem more certain than the things casting them. Dalí gives the low landscape and its ambiguous forms a precise illumination, while their contours suggest more than one possible body. Realistic description becomes a means of sustaining uncertainty. The task is not necessarily to solve the image once, but to notice how one identification displaces another.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Painting, 146 × 114 cm, 1950
works.credit: Pierre Soulages. Peinture 146 x 114 cm, 1950. WikiArt source label: Pierre Soulages Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pierre-soulages/peinture-146-x-114-cm-1950-1950
works.license: Pierre Soulages Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Black occupies much of the surface, but it is not uniform. The broad strokes cross, overlap and leave small pale openings whose shapes alter the surrounding weight. Their edges reveal differences of direction and pressure. Soulages gives the title the restraint of a catalogue description while leaving the relationships among the marks to supply the painting's incident.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Portrait of Erik Satie
works.credit: Suzanne Valadon. Portrait of Erik Satie. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/suzanne-valadon/portrait-of-erik-satie
works.description: The close framing gives little room to a setting beyond Satie's hat and coat. Warmer colours distinguish the face and beard within that dark surround. Valadon concentrates on the angle of the head and the sitter's directed gaze. The portrait can establish a bearing without furnishing the room with attributes intended to explain a composer's whole career.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Still Life with an Antique Bust
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Still life with antique bust. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/still-life-with-antique-bust-1925
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: A bust brings an expectation of solid, modelled volume into a room divided by sharp planes. Around it, orange, white and black areas make depth difficult to follow consistently. Picasso subjects the classical object to the same unstable surroundings as the vessels. Its familiar solidity supplies a point of comparison, not a guarantee that the room will become coherent.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: The Moon-Woman Cuts the Circle
works.credit: The Moon-Woman Cuts the Circle. WikiArt; Jackson Pollock. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Suggestions of figures persist inside the dense lines and coloured marks. They are not cleanly separated from the activity around them, so the eye moves between possible bodies and the surface connecting them. Pollock allows recognition without giving it complete control. Curves and pointed forms can operate as parts of a figure and as interruptions in a larger pattern.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: The Palace of Window Rocks
works.credit: Yves Tanguy. The Palace of Window Rocks. WikiArt source label: Yves Tanguy Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/yves-tanguy/palace-on-windows-rocks
works.license: Yves Tanguy Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The objects have clear shadows but no clear use. Tanguy's low plain provides the rules of a plausible landscape, making the scattered forms appear to stand securely in space. Their unfamiliarity is sharpened by that certainty. A less convincing ground would make them easier to dismiss as free-floating shapes; here they seem to belong somewhere, even when their purpose remains unavailable.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: The Poultry Yard
works.credit: Henri Rousseau. The Poultry Yard. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/henri-rousseau/the-poultry-yard-1898
works.description: Paths, fences and buildings divide the yard into readable compartments. Rousseau gives the setting a pronounced order before the small birds introduce irregular movement within it. The contrast does not require an exotic subject. An ordinary enclosure becomes worth examining because its boundaries are so emphatic and the creatures inside do not follow their straight lines.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: The Serenade
works.credit: The serenade. WikiArt; Pablo Picasso. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: A reclining yellow figure and an upright musician occupy different directions within the angular room. Their relation remains intelligible despite the fractured setting: one performs, the other receives the performance. Picasso separates their positions through colour and bodily arrangement. The image can therefore sustain a recognisable social situation without providing a naturalistic account of either body.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Window, Cour de Rohan
works.credit: Balthus. Window, Cour de Rohan. WikiArt source label: Balthus Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/balthus/window-cour-de-rohan-1951
works.description: The opposite building is not offered directly. It is reached through the open window, past the sill and nearby objects, within a succession of enclosing edges. Balthus makes these intervals more consequential than any activity in the courtyard. The subject is partly the view and partly the measured distance that prevents the view from merging with the room.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Figure
works.credit: Character. WikiArt; Joan Miró. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: A head, curved arms and feet provide enough signs for a body, despite proportions that would not support a person in ordinary space. Miró sets the sharply bounded figure against softer surrounding colour. Gesture remains legible because of the relation among a few parts. Adding anatomical information might clarify the body while weakening the economy of that relation.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: The Blue Room
works.credit: Suzanne Valadon. The Blue Room. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Striped trousers and a blue patterned bed keep clothing and furnishings visibly active around the reclining woman. Books add an ordinary use to the room rather than turning it into an empty setting for a pose. Valadon gives the figure bodily weight without requiring a display of idealised anatomy. The surrounding patterns do not diminish her occupation of the space.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Dada Head
works.credit: Sophie Taeuber-Arp. Dada Head. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The rounded volume promises a head, while its painted geometry declines to complete a naturalistic face. Taeuber-Arp makes these two kinds of information coexist on an object mounted on a narrow stand. The colour does not simply describe the form beneath it. It divides that form according to another order, keeping construction visible alongside resemblance.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: Sky Blue
works.credit: Wassily Kandinsky. Sky Blue. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The gaps are as conspicuous as the floating forms. Each small shape has its own curves, stripes or appendages, yet the continuous blue holds them within one field. Kandinsky avoids making them coalesce into a single mass. Their separateness gives the eye room to move from one internal pattern to another without losing the surrounding space.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

works.title: The King's Sadness
works.credit: Henri Matisse. The King's Sadness. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The yellow instrument and scattered leaf-like shapes bring small movements to the broad coloured areas. Matisse's cut forms suggest bodies and performance without modelling their depth. Clean edges make overlapping activity readable even when the scene is crowded. The title supplies an emotional proposition; the shapes do not have to imitate a sorrowful facial expression to give that proposition a setting.
works.museum: Musée national d’art moderne — Centre Pompidou

closingSections.title: Compare the boundaries
paragraphs: Put Braque's uncertain tabletop beside Balthus's carefully framed view, then return to Kandinsky's open blue field. These are three different accounts of pictorial space. Collection ownership does not establish present display: use the Centre Pompidou's current programme and object records to locate works before travelling.
